newsitem.title: UAE: EU shows it seeks to save Tehran ties - Iran agency.
newsitem.headline: EU shows it seeks to save Tehran ties - Iran agency.

text.p: The European Union has shown it wants to save its trade ties with Iran by allowing the return of ambassadors withdrawn over a row with Tehran, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Tuesday.
"European Union foreign ministers voted Tuesday not to further jeopardise trade links with Iran by deciding to return their ambassadors to Tehran," the agency said.

It was referring to the decisions by the ministers at a meeting in Luxembourg which suspended ministerial ties with Iran in response to a court finding that Iranian leaders had ordered political assassinations in Germany.
The ministers agreed that ambassadors from the 15 member states could return to Tehran if their goverments wished.

"In defiance of U.S. pressure, the EU ministers said that they wanted to have a constructive relationship with Iran, but in an attempt to save face, agreed to suspend ministerial meetings," the agency said in a dispatch from London.
The move was "a political gesture that the EU did not want to further damage ties", the agency said, adding that EU states had "a burgeoning trade gap with Iran".
The United States, which has urged the EU to take a hard line against Tehran, welcomed the EU move, but said it would have preferred a EU decision not to send back its envoys.

There was no official reaction from Iran to the EU decision which came less than three weeks after the Berlin court accused Tehran of ordering the 1992 murder of four Kurdish dissidents. Iran has denied any involvement in the killings.
State-run Tehran radio earlier said any decisions by the EU would fail to affect the Islamic republic because of Iran's extended relations with countries outside Europe.
It said a meeting of foreign ministers of the 10-member regional Economic Cooperation Organisation opening in Tehran on Tuesday was an example of Iran's wide international ties.
The Iranian parliament's foreign relations committee on Tuesday urged the government to end "talks with the EU under whatever names they might be called", Iranian television said.
The EU has suspended its policy of critical dialogue with Iran which has involved talks with Tehran while trying to get the country to move closer to the West.
Iranian newspapers published before Tuesday's EU decision called for curbing economic ties with Europe in favour of other trade partners.

"We have to act more wisely towards Europe and act towards cutting Europe's share and role in the fields of economic and industrial ties and create the situation in which Europe could not even get the idea of striking blows against us," the daily Jomhuri Eslami said.
The English-language Tehran Times said: "In today's world which is based on competition, it is not difficult for Iran to replace its trade partners when (its) values are at stake."
Iranian media and some officials have said Tehran could turn to Asia for its trade as a result of the row with the EU.
